- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >45.0), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a downward bias of 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; cap forecast range within ±3σ of recent 7-day moving average.
- Model underestimates sharp downward corrections after high volatility; add a 1–3% downward adjustment if true outcome drops below 30% of prior 30-day high.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion toward 30–40 range after 10+ days of volatility; apply a 2–5% downward correction after day 10.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast >10% for 3 consecutive days, trigger a “reversion bias” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence or new event triggers.
